title: DR1 tells the user the certification purpose is on the ITAHC; the frontend says it is on the health certificate.

finding.frontend: The hint under "What are the animals certified for?" reads "You'll find this on the health certificate." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/additional-details/copy/copy.en.js:5). The sixteen options below it are identical to DR1's, in the same order and with the same words, so the hint is the only difference in the question.
finding.prototype: The hint on the same question reads "This information can be found on the ITAHC." (app/views/additional-animal-details.html:54). ITAHC is the intra-trade animal health certificate — the document the frontend's hint refers to in general terms — so DR1 names the specific document the user is holding rather than the class of document.
finding.difference: Change the hint under the certification-purpose question to DR1's wording, "This information can be found on the ITAHC." One copy string. Raise it with the designer if the abbreviation is thought to need expanding on first use, but the change is to adopt DR1's wording, not to invent a third.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding that ITAHC and health certificate name different documents here, which would make this a difference in which document the user is sent to rather than a difference in wording.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs — the frontend hint is "You'll find this on the health certificate." at fe-additional-details.html:127 and DR1's is "This information can be found on the ITAHC." at dr1-additional-animal-details.html:275 — plus both full-page screenshots and both cited lines, which resolve exactly. Ran the falsifier by reading where each side's options come from: DR1's sixteen are a flat commodity-independent list in app/data/certification-purposes.js, and they match the frontend's word for word and in order, so the two hints describe the same question and only the document name differs. CORRECT.
